claims.text: No ASGI app of the MCP server is handed out, locked or not, so a saved app cannot be served by an ASGI runner with lifespan off (R29, P18).
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q -m invariants -k "p18 and asgi or p5_a_custom or p5_no_prompt"

claims.text: With the lock off, run('sse'), run('streamable-http'), run_sse_async and run_streamable_http_async still build their app and hand it to uvicorn after the lock check; the app is still refused outside those calls (R53). Custom policy rule ids and descriptions never reach the prompt (P5, R30). Monzo ids beginning . or : import again.
Lint, compile and offline evals pass.
claims.proof_cmd: ruff check src tests evals && python -m compileall -q src && python evals/run_evals.py
claims.proof_output: All checks passed! ... 9/9 memos fully grounded; model = fake

dispositions.finding: major src/cma/mcp_server.py:89 (P18/R29): a saved ASGI app can bind under the lock if the ASGI runner skips lifespan.
dispositions.evidence: Commit 478e616 removed LockedASGIApp: sse_app()/streamable_http_app() raise NoASGIApp (an OfflineLockError) whatever the lock, so no app exists to serve before a lock check. Test: test_p18_no_asgi_app_is_handed_out_whatever_the_lock (invariants). That commit also broke the SDK's own HTTP run methods, which call self.sse_app(); b34945b allows the build only inside our run_sse_async/run_streamable_http_async, after require_unlocked, through a ContextVar. New test test_http_transports_still_start_when_lock_is_off (contracts) failed before b34945b and passes now.

dispositions.finding: major src/cma/graph.py:174 (R30/P5): custom policy descriptions are copied verbatim into hosted prompts.
dispositions.evidence: rules_table(for_prompt=True) sends a description only when it equals the shipped policy's text for that rule id, and otherwise sends '(custom rule)' (478e616). The rule id is free text too. Before b34945b, test_p5_a_custom_policys_rule_id_or_description_never_reaches_the_prompt[id] failed with the sentinel id in the prompt. Since b34945b the prompt sends only ids matching R\d{1,4} and replaces any other with '(custom id)'. Both P5 custom-policy tests pass (invariants).

dispositions.finding: minor src/cma/mcp_server.py:193 (R30): transactions_for with include_descriptions=True no longer returns untrusted_description.
dispositions.evidence: No code change. R34 says payer text is never sent to a model, and an MCP client is a model, so returning the field would break R34/R30. The option is still accepted, and each row says description_withheld: True (tests/test_mcp_paths.py:72). The R53 tension is noted for the owner.

dispositions.finding: minor src/cma/importers/monzo.py:42: the formula guard also rejects Transaction IDs beginning with . or :.
dispositions.evidence: SAFE_ID now refuses only a leading '-'. '=', '+' and '@' were never in the id charset. New contracts test test_ids_the_previous_release_took_still_import ('.tx', ':tx', 'tx_1.2:3-4') passes. test_formula_leading_transaction_id_is_refused now covers -2-3, -tx, =1+1, +1 and @x.

dispositions.finding: minor src/cma/graph.py:242 (R29): the claim that the previous package ignores the additive egress key is unproven.
dispositions.evidence: Claim withdrawn: this claim.json makes no reverse-compatibility claim about the egress key. Only the current code reading older state is covered by existing tests.

notes: HEAD before this run was 478e616, an unreviewed fix for verify-122's two majors. This run found and fixed two gaps in it: the HTTP/SSE run methods could not start at all, and custom rule ids still reached the prompt. Open point: the include_descriptions field removal trades R53 field stability for R34; the owner may want that stated.
